title: Lakes, warehouses and lakehouses: architecture
summary: How the parts of this lesson fit together.

steps.n: Sources are applications, databases and event streams.
A warehouse stores structured tables with strong performance and governance, but storage and compute are often tied together.
Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake add a metadata layer over files in object storage.
A common layout has a raw zone that keeps data exactly as received, a cleaned zone with typed and deduplicated tables, and a curated zone with business ready models.
Batch jobs process large sets on a schedule and are simple and cheap.
Confirm the outcome with a metric, a query or a test, and write down what changed so the next person can repeat it.

title: Failure and recovery: A dashboard that showed half of yesterday
summary: A realistic failure and the way back.

steps.n: The system works and the team relies on it, so nobody is watching this particular risk closely.
Two jobs wrote to the same folder and a report read partial files.
An operator runs a command such as: aws s3 ls s3://corp-lake/curated/orders/dt=2026-11-20/ --summarize | tail -2
A compaction job and a load job wrote to the same partition while a dashboard query ran, so the report counted some files twice and missed others.
Moving the tables to Iceberg gave atomic commits, so readers see either the old snapshot or the new one, never a mix.
The team closes the gap: avoid this mistake: Writing files straight into folders that others read.
The incident is reviewed for system and process causes and the runbook is updated so the next responder finds the answer faster.

title: Kafka operations: topics, partitions and consumer groups
summary: How the parts of this lesson fit together.

steps.n: A topic is split into partitions, and order is guaranteed only inside one partition.
Each partition has a leader and followers.
Consumers in a group share partitions, and each commits the offset it has processed.
Retention deletes data by age or size, for example seven days.
Watch disk, network and request latency per broker.
Confirm the outcome with a metric, a query or a test, and write down what changed so the next person can repeat it.

title: Failure and recovery: Consumers fell behind and then lost messages
summary: A realistic failure and the way back.

steps.n: The system works and the team relies on it, so nobody is watching this particular risk closely.
A consumer group was down over a weekend and its offsets expired from the topic.
An operator runs a command such as: kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server broker1:9092 --describe --group billing
Retention on the topic was two days and the group was down for three, so the oldest messages were deleted before they were read and the group restarted from the earliest available offset.
The team raised retention to seven days for billing topics and added an alert on lag older than one hour.
The team closes the gap: avoid this mistake: acks=1 for important data.
The incident is reviewed for system and process causes and the runbook is updated so the next responder finds the answer faster.

title: Batch orchestration with Airflow
summary: How the parts of this lesson fit together.

steps.n: A DAG is a graph of tasks with no cycles.
A task is idempotent when running it twice for the same interval gives the same result.
Set retries with a delay and an execution timeout so a stuck task does not hold a slot forever.
A backfill reruns a range of past intervals after a fix or a new DAG.
The scheduler, the metadata database, the executor and the workers all need monitoring.
Confirm the outcome with a metric, a query or a test, and write down what changed so the next person can repeat it.

title: Failure and recovery: A retry that doubled yesterday revenue
summary: A realistic failure and the way back.

steps.n: The system works and the team relies on it, so nobody is watching this particular risk closely.
A failed load task retried and appended rows a second time.
An operator runs a command such as: psql -h warehouse -c "select dt, count(*) from fact_sales where dt = '2026-11-20' group by dt"
The task appended rows each time it ran, so a retry after a timeout loaded the same day twice and the report showed double revenue.
The team changed the task to overwrite the date partition, added a row count check against the source and marked the load task as idempotent in the DAG documentation.
The team closes the gap: avoid this mistake: Append only tasks that cannot be retried.
The incident is reviewed for system and process causes and the runbook is updated so the next responder finds the answer faster.

title: Spark and distributed processing for operators
summary: How the parts of this lesson fit together.

steps.n: The driver turns code into a plan, splits it into stages and sends tasks to executors.
A shuffle writes data to disk, sends it over the network and reads it back.
Skew means a few keys hold most of the data, so one task runs for an hour while the others finish in seconds.
An executor out of memory is often caused by a skewed partition, a large collect to the driver or too many cores sharing one heap.
The stages tab shows task duration spread, shuffle read and write and spilled data.
Confirm the outcome with a metric, a query or a test, and write down what changed so the next person can repeat it.

title: Failure and recovery: One task ran for three hours
summary: A realistic failure and the way back.

steps.n: The system works and the team relies on it, so nobody is watching this particular risk closely.
A nightly join was stuck on a single task while the rest of the cluster sat idle.
An operator runs a command such as: curl -s http://spark-history:18080/api/v1/applications/app-2026/stages/7/taskSummary | head -c 300
The median task took two seconds and the slowest took three hours because one customer id held most of the rows.
Enabling adaptive skew handling and salting the key for that join spread the work and brought the stage down to a few minutes.
The team closes the gap: avoid this mistake: Adding executors to fix a skewed join.
The incident is reviewed for system and process causes and the runbook is updated so the next responder finds the answer faster.

title: Data quality, contracts and lineage
summary: How the parts of this lesson fit together.

steps.n: Freshness asks whether the table was updated on time.
A data contract is an agreement between the team that produces a dataset and the teams that use it.
Lineage records which datasets and jobs feed which others, for example with OpenLineage.
Run checks at ingestion to reject or quarantine bad input, and after transformations to protect curated tables.
Every important dataset has an owner and a channel.

title: Failure and recovery: A renamed column that broke the revenue report
summary: A realistic failure and the way back.

steps.n: The system works and the team relies on it, so nobody is watching this particular risk closely.
A producer renamed a column and the finance dashboard showed zeros.
An operator runs a command such as: python -c "print('null share of revenue_usd: 100 percent')"
A source team renamed amount to revenue_usd, the transformation selected the old name and filled it with nulls, and no check noticed.
After the incident the team added a schema contract check in the producer pipeline, a null share test on the finance table and lineage so the producer could see which reports depended on the column.
The team closes the gap: avoid this mistake: Testing nothing until a user complains.
The incident is reviewed for system and process causes and the runbook is updated so the next responder finds the answer faster.

title: Governance, cost and reliability of data platforms
summary: How the parts of this lesson fit together.

steps.n: Classify data as public, internal or sensitive and apply rules to each class.
Keep data only as long as there is a reason to.
Storage cost grows quietly: duplicate copies, old partitions and tiny files.
Treat important datasets as products with service levels: freshness within a time, completeness above a threshold and a stated recovery time.
Run an on call rotation for the platform with runbooks for stuck pipelines, lagging streams and failed loads.
Confirm the outcome with a metric, a query or a test, and write down what changed so the next person can repeat it.

title: Failure and recovery: A query that cost more than the team monthly budget
summary: A realistic failure and the way back.

steps.n: The system works and the team relies on it, so nobody is watching this particular risk closely.
One analyst unbounded query scanned a petabyte of raw logs.
An operator runs a command such as: bq query --dry_run --use_legacy_sql=false 'select count(*) from raw.events'
There was no limit on bytes scanned and the raw table was not partitioned, so a full scan ran against the entire history.
The platform team added a per user scan limit, partitioned the table by date, required a partition filter and showed dry run estimates in the query tool.
The team closes the gap: avoid this mistake: Granting access per person instead of by role.
The incident is reviewed for system and process causes and the runbook is updated so the next responder finds the answer faster.
